boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Dominican University of California
boards.description: A guide to the essential late-night food and study spots for students at Dominican University of California, featuring on-campus options and local San Rafael favorites.

cards.title: Caleruega Dining Hall
cards.subtitle: On-Campus Main Dining
cards.notes: Visit the main campus hub for late-night mobile orders through the DU To Go service, providing hot meals until 9:00 PM on weekdays.
cards.short_summary: The primary on-campus dining facility offering a variety of food concepts and a dedicated late-evening mobile ordering service.
cards.evidence_claim: Caleruega Dining Hall offers 'DU To Go' mobile ordering Monday through Thursday from 2:00 PM to 9:00 PM.
cards.source_title: Dining Locations - Dominican University Dining
cards.access_notes: Open for DU To Go until 9:00 PM Mon-Thu; until 8:00 PM Fri-Sun.

cards.title: Chilly's Café
cards.subtitle: Guzman Hall Coffee Spot
cards.notes: Stop by Guzman Hall for coffee, tea, and desserts in a social campus setting that stays open until 8:00 PM most weeknights.
cards.short_summary: An independent on-campus café known for its specialty coffee, Arabic savories like kunafa, and evening study atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: Chilly's Café is located at Guzman Hall and is open Monday through Thursday until 8:00 PM.
cards.source_title: Chilly's Café - San Rafael, CA | joe coffee
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Thursday 7:45 AM - 8:00 PM; Friday 10:00 AM - 2:00 PM.

cards.title: Jack in the Box
cards.subtitle: 24-Hour Drive-Thru
cards.notes: Head to 2nd Street for a full menu available 24/7, including breakfast items and late-night munchie meals just a short drive from campus.
cards.short_summary: A reliable 24-hour fast-food destination in downtown San Rafael serving burgers, tacos, and breakfast all day.
cards.evidence_claim: The Jack in the Box at 1814 2nd St in San Rafael operates its drive-thru and lobby 24 hours a day.
cards.source_title: Jack In The Box in San Rafael, California
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru and lobby are open 24 hours daily.

cards.title: 7-Eleven
cards.subtitle: 24/7 Convenience Hub
cards.notes: Grab quick snacks, hot food, or beverages at any hour from this downtown convenience staple located near the transit center.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour convenience store providing essential snacks and quick-service hot food for late-night study sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: The 7-Eleven at 703 B St in San Rafael is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
cards.source_title: 703 B St San Rafael CA 94901 - 7-Eleven
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 for walk-in and mobile checkout.

cards.title: Taco Bell
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Mexican Fast Food
cards.notes: Drive over for classic tacos and burritos available until midnight daily, perfect for a post-study snack run.
cards.short_summary: A popular late-night fast-food chain in San Rafael offering a customizable menu of Mexican-inspired favorites.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell at 555 Second Street in San Rafael is open until 12:00 AM daily.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell in San Rafael, CA - 555 Second Street
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 10:00 AM to 12:00 AM.

cards.title: Safeway
cards.subtitle: Midnight Grocery Run
cards.notes: Stock up on dorm essentials or grab a late-night deli sandwich at this supermarket that stays open until midnight.
cards.short_summary: A large grocery store in downtown San Rafael providing a wide selection of food and household items until late evening.
cards.evidence_claim: The Safeway at 700 B St in San Rafael is open daily until 12:00 AM.
cards.source_title: Safeway Locations in San Rafael, CA
cards.access_notes: Store hours are 6:00 AM to 12:00 AM daily.

cards.title: In-N-Out Burger
cards.subtitle: California Classic Late-Night
cards.notes: Join the late-night queue for a Double-Double and animal-style fries at this iconic regional chain open until 1:00 AM or later.
cards.short_summary: A quintessential California burger joint located just south of campus, serving fresh burgers and shakes late into the night.
cards.evidence_claim: In-N-Out Burger locations typically stay open until 1:00 AM on weeknights and 1:30 AM on weekends.
cards.source_title: Locations - In-N-Out Burger
cards.access_notes: Open Sun-Thu until 1:00 AM; Fri-Sat until 1:30 AM.

cards.title: Denny's
cards.subtitle: 24-Hour Diner Classics
cards.notes: Gather for a Grand Slam or late-night burger at this 24-hour diner, a staple for students needing a place to eat at any hour.
cards.short_summary: A classic American diner offering full breakfast, lunch, and dinner menus 24 hours a day in San Rafael.
cards.evidence_claim: Denny's is a 24-hour diner and breakfast restaurant with locations serving late-night food 24/7.
cards.source_title: Denny's: 24-Hour Diner and Breakfast Restaurant
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily.

cards.title: Cyber Café
cards.subtitle: Archbishop Alemany Library
cards.notes: Utilize this library-based café for grab-and-go snacks and study space during regular library operating hours.
cards.short_summary: Located in the lower level of the library, this café offers sandwiches, salads, and a convenient place to study on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cyber Café is located in the lower level of the library and is open Monday through Friday until 5:00 PM during regular sessions.
cards.source_title: Dining Locations - Dominican University Dining
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 8:00 AM - 5:00 PM; closed weekends.

cards.title: Black Bear Diner
cards.subtitle: Hearty Evening Meals
cards.notes: Enjoy large portions of comfort food until 9:00 PM or 10:00 PM, making it a great spot for a late dinner near campus.
cards.short_summary: A bear-themed diner known for its sizable helpings of home-style food and friendly service in San Rafael.
cards.evidence_claim: Black Bear Diner in San Rafael is open until 9:00 PM Sunday-Thursday and until 10:00 PM Friday-Saturday.
cards.source_title: San Rafael | Black Bear Diner
cards.access_notes: Open Mon-Thu/Sun until 9:00 PM; Fri-Sat until 10:00 PM.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional student spaces and historic corners of Dominican University of California that define daily life beyond the standard tour route.

cards.title: Learning Commons Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Collaborative hubs in the library
cards.notes: Reserve the large or small study rooms for group projects. These spaces feature smart TVs and whiteboards for collaborative work sessions.

cards.evidence_claim: The Archbishop Alemany Library provides quiet study spaces and reservable rooms for group study, including a Large Study Room and Small Study Room.

cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; room reservations are managed through the library's online system.

cards.title: Edgehill Mansion Student Hub

cards.title: Caleruega Dining Hall
cards.subtitle: The primary campus social eatery
cards.notes: Grab a meal at the Chef's Table or build a custom waffle. This is the main social hub for resident and commuter students alike.
cards.short_summary: The university's main dining facility offering diverse food concepts and a central gathering space.
cards.evidence_claim: Caleruega Dining Hall is the main dining hall for student meals and is open to all members of the campus community.
cards.source_title: Dining | Dominican University of California

cards.title: Fanjeaux Hall Student Lounge

cards.short_summary: A multi-use student lounge located on the ground floor of the ivy-covered Fanjeaux Hall.

cards.title: Conlan Center Weight Room
cards.subtitle: Campus fitness and recreation

cards.evidence_claim: The Conlan Center features a weight room with cardio machines and free weights available to the Dominican community.
cards.source_title: Weight and Fitness Center - Dominican University of California Athletics
cards.access_notes: Requires a valid Dominican ID for entry; check athletics website for current operating hours.

cards.title: Meadowlands Hall Grounds
cards.subtitle: Quiet Victorian estate setting
cards.notes: Walk the grounds of this 1888 Victorian mansion. It's a peaceful spot on the edge of campus for a quiet break between classes.
cards.short_summary: A historic Victorian mansion and surrounding grounds used for academic and administrative purposes.
cards.evidence_claim: Meadowlands Hall is an elegant Victorian mansion built in 1888 located on the Dominican campus.
cards.source_title: Our Campus | Dominican University of California
cards.access_notes: Outdoor grounds are accessible; building access is limited to academic and administrative hours.

cards.title: Guzman Gazebo
cards.subtitle: Outdoor campus landmark
cards.notes: Meet friends at the gazebo near Guzman Hall. It's a recognizable landmark often used as a gathering point for outdoor study.
cards.short_summary: A central outdoor gazebo located near Guzman Hall, serving as a student meeting spot.
cards.evidence_claim: The Guzman Gazebo is listed as a campus landmark on the official university directory and map.
cards.source_title: Campus Map and Directory - Dominican University of California
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 as an outdoor campus space.

cards.title: Angelico Hall Performance Space
cards.subtitle: Campus cultural and music center
cards.notes: Attend a recital or lecture in this historic hall. It's the primary venue for the university's music programs and public events.
cards.short_summary: A historic performance hall that serves as the center for music and cultural events on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Angelico Hall is a key campus building housing performance spaces and music-related facilities.
cards.source_title: Campus Map and Directory - Dominican University of California
cards.access_notes: Access typically restricted to scheduled events and music department activities.

cards.title: Student Success Center
cards.subtitle: Academic support and advising
cards.notes: Head to Bertrand Hall for tutoring, advising, and career services. It's the go-to spot for academic planning and support.
cards.short_summary: A central administrative and academic building housing the Student Success Center and Tutoring services.
cards.evidence_claim: Bertrand Hall houses the Student Success Center, Tutoring and Learning Center, and the Registrar.
cards.source_title: Campus Map and Directory - Dominican University of California
cards.access_notes: Open during university business hours.

cards.title: Forest Meadows Amphitheater
cards.subtitle: Outdoor performance venue
cards.notes: Check out this outdoor venue for campus events and the Marin Shakespeare Company performances during the summer.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor amphitheater located on the campus perimeter used for university and community performances.
cards.evidence_claim: The Forest Meadows Amphitheater is a designated facility on the Dominican campus map.
cards.source_title: Campus Map and Directory - Dominican University of California
cards.access_notes: Open for scheduled events; grounds are generally accessible during daylight hours.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Explore free social spaces and activities at Dominican University of California, from historic mansion grounds to student-designed gardens and art galleries.

cards.title: Study at Alemany Library
cards.subtitle: 50 Acacia Avenue
cards.notes: Access quiet study zones and group seminar rooms. Visitors must present a valid photo ID and sign in at the front desk to enter the main library floors.
cards.short_summary: The central campus library offering quiet study spaces and research resources.
cards.evidence_claim: All are welcome to visit Archbishop Alemany Library. To enter the main library visitors must have a valid photo ID and sign in.
cards.source_title: Who can use the Library? - Ask the Library
cards.access_notes: Open to the public with photo ID sign-in; student-only access for WiFi and printing.

cards.title: View Art at Goodman Gallery
cards.subtitle: Alemany Library, 1st Floor
cards.notes: Visit this gallery located inside the library to see rotating exhibits by students and community artists. It features floor-to-ceiling windows and updated lighting.
cards.short_summary: A campus art gallery showcasing student and community works with free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library houses the Barbara D. Goodman Art Gallery and the Community Gallery... ADMISSION INFO. Free
cards.source_title: Barbara D. Goodman Art Gallery - MarinArts
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; free and open to the public.

cards.title: Relax in the Pollinator Garden
cards.subtitle: Next to Albertus Magnus Hall
cards.notes: Walk through five distinct plant islands designed to support local bees and butterflies. This student-developed space uses harvested rainwater for irrigation.
cards.short_summary: A sustainable campus garden featuring native plants and habitats for local pollinators.
cards.evidence_claim: The garden, located next to Albertus Magnus, is named in honor of the late Daniel Stralka... A public space and student research garden.
cards.source_title: Pollinator Garden At Dominican Gains Campus-Wide Support
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public space accessible daily.

cards.title: Explore Edgehill Mansion Grounds
cards.subtitle: 75 Magnolia Avenue
cards.notes: Stroll past this 1887 Queen Anne Victorian mansion. While it houses administrative offices, the surrounding grounds offer a historic park-like setting.
cards.short_summary: Historic Victorian mansion grounds offering scenic walks and architectural views.
cards.evidence_claim: Edgehill Mansion, an elegant Queen Anne Victorian, was constructed in 1887... Edgehill Mansion houses Campus Ministry, Student Life and more.
cards.source_title: Our Campus | Dominican University of California
cards.access_notes: Exterior grounds are open to the public; interior houses university offices.

cards.title: Meet at Guzman Gazebo
cards.subtitle: Near Guzman Hall
cards.notes: Gather at this central campus landmark for outdoor socializing. It is located in the meadow area between Guzman Hall and Meadowlands Hall.
cards.short_summary: A traditional outdoor gazebo used as a central campus meeting point.
cards.evidence_claim: The campus map identifies the 'Guzman Gazebo' as a distinct landmark near Guzman Hall and Meadowlands Hall.
cards.source_title: Visitor's Guide - Dominican University of California
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark accessible to students and visitors.

cards.title: Attend Little Penguins Story Time
cards.subtitle: Alemany Library Front Steps
cards.notes: Join a community reading event on the first and third Friday of every month. It is free and open to all ages, moving inside the library in case of rain.
cards.short_summary: A free, public bi-monthly story time event held on the library steps.
cards.evidence_claim: Join us on the front steps of Archbishop Alemany Library from 10 - 10:30 a.m. on the first and third Friday of every month. Free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Community and Neighborhood Engagement
cards.access_notes: Held 10:00-10:30 AM on select Fridays; open to the general public.

cards.title: Work Out at Conlan Center
cards.subtitle: 1475 Grand Avenue
cards.notes: Use the fitness center, basketball courts, and swimming pool. Access is included for all current students with a valid Penguin Pass ID card.
cards.short_summary: The campus recreation hub providing free fitness and sports access for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Penguin Pass ID Card allows you to: Access computer labs, the Conlan Recreation Center and the residence halls.
cards.source_title: Penguin Pass | Dominican University of California
cards.access_notes: Student-only access; requires valid Penguin Pass ID card.

cards.title: Explore San Marco Gallery
cards.subtitle: Archbishop Alemany Library
cards.notes: View fine art exhibitions in this professional gallery space. It is open during normal library hours and serves as a venue for both student and professional artists.
cards.short_summary: A professional art gallery within the library featuring rotating exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: San Marco Gallery, Alemany Library... Hours: During normal library hours. Admission is free.
cards.source_title: Dominican University of California, San Marco Gallery
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; free public access.

cards.title: Hang at the SIRC
cards.subtitle: Edgehill Mansion, Garden Level
cards.notes: Check out board games, art supplies, or a firepit for club events. This hub is designed for student organizations to gather and plan activities.
cards.short_summary: A resource hub for students to access games, supplies, and social equipment.
cards.evidence_claim: Student clubs and organizations can come to the SIRC and have access to supplies... Students can also check out board games, art supplies and even a firepit.
cards.source_title: Get Involved on Campus | Dominican University
cards.access_notes: Student-only resource center located in Edgehill Mansion.

cards.title: Picnic at Forest Meadows
cards.subtitle: 890 Belle Avenue
cards.notes: Bring a blanket and a meal to this outdoor amphitheater surrounded by trees. It opens one hour before performances for public picnicking.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor sylvan amphitheater open for public picnicking before events.
cards.evidence_claim: The amphitheater opens one hour prior to show time for picnicking. Audiences are encouraged to bring picnics... Parking is free.
cards.source_title: Forest Meadows Amphitheater, Upcoming Events in San Rafael
cards.access_notes: Open to the public one hour before scheduled performances; free parking available.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Discover the unique rituals and long-standing traditions that define the student experience at Dominican University of California, from symbolic shield ceremonies to the legacy of the Penguin mascot.

cards.title: Shield Day
cards.subtitle: A Century-Old Welcome for Freshmen
cards.notes: Seniors present incoming freshmen with a hand-illustrated wooden shield featuring an inspirational motto to guide them through their college years.
cards.short_summary: A welcoming ceremony where seniors gift freshmen unique wooden shields with mottos.
cards.evidence_claim: The tradition began in the early 1920s and involves seniors greeting freshmen with an illustrated shield carved in wood reflecting an inspirational motto.
cards.source_title: Traditions | Dominican University of California
cards.access_notes: Held annually during the fall semester as part of Convocation.

cards.title: Candle and Rose Ceremony
cards.subtitle: The Light of Truth and Love
cards.notes: Graduating seniors carry lit candles and exchange them for roses with a chosen partner, symbolizing the passing of truth and the receipt of love.
cards.short_summary: A twilight procession where graduates exchange candles for roses with mentors or friends.
cards.evidence_claim: First held in 1928, the ceremony involves a procession from the upper cloister walk to the Quad where candles and roses are exchanged.
cards.source_title: So Proudly Dominican: Traditions at DU
cards.access_notes: Takes place on the eve of Commencement in the campus Quad.

cards.title: Paint the Dog
cards.subtitle: Senior Year Rebellion Turned Tradition
cards.notes: Seniors gather on the Meadowlands lawn to leave their mark by painting the campus dog statue before they graduate.
cards.short_summary: A senior tradition where students paint the campus dog statue on Meadowlands lawn.
cards.evidence_claim: What began as a spirited act of rebellion is now an official tradition where seniors gather on Meadowlands lawn to mark the campus dog statue.
cards.source_title: Traditions | Dominican University of California
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually during the spring semester for graduating seniors.

cards.title: The Penguin Mascot
cards.subtitle: Inspired by the Dominican Sisters
cards.notes: Students in the 1970s chose the penguin as a mascot because the black-and-white habits of the Dominican Sisters resembled the birds.
cards.short_summary: The university mascot, Chilly the Penguin, was inspired by the sisters' habits.
cards.evidence_claim: In the 1970s, students petitioned to change the mascot from a hound to a penguin because the sisters' habits resembled penguins.
cards.source_title: The Story of the Penguin Mascot | Dominican Alumni
cards.access_notes: Visible at athletic events and campus spirit days throughout the year.

cards.title: Christmas Tree Lighting
cards.subtitle: Holiday Cheer at Angelico Hall
cards.notes: The community gathers outside Angelico Hall to light a 60-foot Blue Spanish Fir, accompanied by caroling and cookie decorating.
cards.short_summary: An annual holiday event featuring the lighting of a massive fir tree and caroling.
cards.evidence_claim: The community gathers to light the tree outside Angelico Hall with caroling and cookie decorating to mark the holiday season.
cards.source_title: Seniors Represent Ideals At Holiday Tree Lighting
cards.access_notes: Held annually in early December; open to the public.

cards.title: Bagpiper Procession
cards.subtitle: A Musical Lead for Graduates
cards.notes: Commencement ceremonies at Dominican are traditionally led by a bagpiper, guiding the graduates to Forest Meadows Field.
cards.short_summary: The traditional use of a bagpiper to lead the graduation procession.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dominican tradition includes a procession led by a bagpiper during the Commencement ceremony.
cards.source_title: Traditions | Dominican University of California
cards.access_notes: Occurs during the spring and fall Commencement ceremonies.

cards.title: The Shield Room
cards.subtitle: A Gallery of Class Mottos
cards.notes: Visit the Shield Room to see the collection of hand-carved wooden shields from every graduating class dating back to the 1920s.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated space on campus displaying historic class shields and mottos.
cards.evidence_claim: All of Dominican's shields, dating back to the early 1920s, are displayed on campus in the Meadowlands Residence Hall and the Shield Room.
cards.source_title: Traditions | Dominican University of California
cards.access_notes: Located within Meadowlands Hall; accessible during standard building hours.

cards.title: Chilly's Fall Fest
cards.subtitle: Homecoming, Dominican-Style
cards.notes: A carnival-style celebration on the Meadowlands Lawn featuring rides, food trucks, and games for the entire campus community.
cards.short_summary: The university's annual homecoming festival held on the Meadowlands Lawn.
cards.evidence_claim: Chilly's Fall Fest and Carnival is described as 'Homecoming, Dominican-style' with rides, music, and games on Meadowlands Lawn.
cards.source_title: Convocation and Family Weekend | Dominican University of California
cards.access_notes: Held annually in October during Family Weekend.

cards.title: Senior Thesis Tradition
cards.subtitle: The Capstone of the Dominican Experience
cards.notes: Every undergraduate completes a senior thesis or project, a rigorous academic tradition that culminates in a public presentation of their research.
cards.short_summary: A mandatory capstone project for all seniors involving original research or creative work.
cards.evidence_claim: The senior thesis gives students an opportunity to explore in-depth issues, taking forms like research documents, novels, or original art.
cards.source_title: Senior Theses | Dominican Scholar
cards.access_notes: Theses are archived in the Dominican Scholar and presented during the spring semester.

cards.title: Baccalaureate Mass
cards.subtitle: A Heritage of Faith
cards.notes: Held the day before Commencement, this Mass reflects the university's Catholic heritage and the founding Dominican Sisters' values.
cards.short_summary: A traditional religious service held for graduates and their families before Commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: Held the day prior to Commencement, the Baccalaureate Mass is a unique Dominican tradition reflecting its Catholic heritage.
cards.source_title: Traditions | Dominican University of California
cards.access_notes: Typically held in Angelico Hall or a local chapel during graduation weekend.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Dominican University of California, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A guide to your first few days as a Penguin, from move-in at the Conlan Center to exploring the historic grounds of San Rafael.

cards.title: Check In at the Igloo
cards.subtitle: Move-In Day Kickoff
cards.notes: Start your journey at the Conlan Center gymnasium for orientation check-in and move-in instructions. It is the hub for Penguin athletics and major campus gatherings.
cards.short_summary: The primary athletic facility and check-in point for new student orientation.
cards.evidence_claim: New students check in at the Conlan Recreation Center gymnasium to begin the move-in process and orientation.
cards.source_title: New Student Orientation | Dominican University of California
cards.access_notes: Open for scheduled orientation events; regular gym hours vary by semester.

cards.title: First Meal on the Plaza
cards.subtitle: Dining and Community
cards.notes: Head to Caleruega for your first campus meal. The outdoor patio is a popular spot for meeting fellow new students during the orientation mixer.
cards.short_summary: The main campus dining facility offering a variety of food concepts and outdoor seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Caleruega Dining Hall is the main dining hall for student meals and hosts orientation mixers on its outdoor patio.
cards.source_title: Dining | Dominican University of California
cards.access_notes: Standard meal hours apply; typically open for breakfast, lunch, and dinner.

cards.title: The University Welcome
cards.subtitle: Orientation Sessions
cards.notes: Attend the Student Life and Engagement sessions in this historic concert hall. It is a central venue for lectures and performing arts on campus.
cards.short_summary: A historic concert hall used for major university presentations and cultural events.
cards.evidence_claim: Orientation sessions, including Student Life and Engagement, are held in Angelico Hall.
cards.source_title: New Student Orientation | Dominican University of California
cards.access_notes: Access is typically limited to scheduled events and performances.

cards.title: Explore Downtown San Rafael
cards.subtitle: Thursday Night Tradition
cards.notes: Take the university shuttle to Fourth Street for the local farmers market. It's a great way to experience the local community and grab fresh snacks.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal evening market in downtown San Rafael featuring local vendors and food.
cards.evidence_claim: The orientation program includes a visit to the Downtown Farmers Market in San Rafael with shuttle service provided.
cards.source_title: New Student Orientation | Dominican University of California
cards.access_notes: Seasonal on Thursday evenings; check local schedules for exact dates.

cards.title: Catch a Movie Downtown
cards.subtitle: Orientation Night Out
cards.notes: Enjoy a film at this restored theater in downtown San Rafael. Tickets are often provided for new students during the first weekend's evening activities.
cards.short_summary: A historic cinema in downtown San Rafael that hosts student movie nights.
cards.evidence_claim: New students attend a movie at the Smith Rafael Film Center as part of the orientation schedule.
cards.source_title: New Student Orientation | Dominican University of California
cards.access_notes: Open for scheduled screenings; shuttle service often provided from campus.

cards.title: Find Your Study Spot
cards.subtitle: Academic Hub
cards.notes: Visit the library lawn for orientation events or head inside to explore the quiet study spaces and research resources available to all students.
cards.short_summary: The main campus library providing research assistance and diverse study environments.
cards.evidence_claim: The Alemany Library Lawn serves as a pickup location for shuttles and a site for orientation activities.
cards.source_title: The Archbishop Alemany Library - Dominican University of California
cards.access_notes: Hours vary by semester; check the library website for current opening times.

cards.title: Visit the Office of Student Engagement
cards.subtitle: Historic Campus Landmark
cards.notes: Located on the second floor of this historic mansion, the Office of Student Engagement is where you can learn about joining clubs and organizations.
cards.short_summary: A historic building housing student life offices and serving as a landmark on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Office of Student Engagement is located on the second floor of Edgehill Mansion.
cards.source_title: Getting Involved | Dominican University of California
cards.access_notes: Open during standard business hours for student services.

cards.title: Afternoon at the Field
cards.subtitle: Outdoor Recreation
cards.notes: Walk over to Forest Meadows for fresh air or to watch a soccer match. This expansive green space is also the site of the university's commencement.
cards.short_summary: A large outdoor athletic field used for sports and major university ceremonies.
cards.evidence_claim: Forest Meadows Field is used for athletic events and the annual commencement ceremony.
cards.source_title: Dominican to Celebrate Spring Commencement, May 11
cards.access_notes: Open for public use when not reserved for athletic practices or events.

cards.title: Discover Campus History
cards.subtitle: Academic Landmark
cards.notes: Named after St. Dominic de Guzman, this building is a cornerstone of campus. Explore the nearby gazebo for a quiet spot between orientation sessions.
cards.short_summary: A central academic building and landmark named after the university's namesake.
cards.evidence_claim: Guzman Hall is named after Dominic de Guzman and is a key academic building on campus.
cards.source_title: Growing Strong Lianni Castro.docx - Dominican Scholar
cards.access_notes: Open during academic hours; gazebo is accessible outdoors.

cards.title: A Moment of Zen
cards.subtitle: Sister City Gift
cards.notes: Visit this tranquil garden, a gift from San Rafael's sister city, Kushiro. It is a peaceful spot for reflection before classes begin on Monday.
cards.short_summary: A traditional Japanese garden located on campus, symbolizing international friendship.
cards.evidence_claim: The Chidori-en Japanese Garden is a feature of the Dominican campus, gifted by the sister city of Kushiro.
cards.source_title: Campus Map and Directory - Dominican University of California
cards.access_notes: Outdoor garden area; generally accessible during daylight hours.
